why: Lean into Zada: the deck is built on copying a single-target spell across the board and runs only FOUR drawing fodder cantrips out of the 16 that exist in mono-red. This pass takes fodder from 4 to 10, protection from 2 to 4 (Zada is a 3-mana 3/3 the whole deck depends on), and adds the two storm cards that actually convert. Slots come from the ramp surplus (15 vs target 10-12) and the 4-5 drop Goblin bodies, not from the token makers.

commits.message: Fodder 4 -> 10, protection 2 -> 4, two real storm cards; slots from the ramp surplus and the 5-drops.
Pass 2: CONVERSION. Pass 1 tripled card draw and did not move the kill rate, so this adds per-cast damage, a board-wide pump with buyback, and ward protection.
Pass 3: the STORM axis. The ritual leg of the storm target, which pass 1 damaged by cutting Glimpse the Impossible and Spreading Insurrection.

Restore Spreading Insurrection: cutting it stranded a name in the storm target's payoff leg, which the tracked-artifact validator caught. Galvanic Relay comes out with it as the paired half of that swap.
Pass 4: pump count 1 -> 3, spell-for-spell. Bodies are the copy count and the branch was already behind the champion until turn 9, so no creature comes out for this.

Pass 5 (Alex's read): swap two draw-only cantrips for buff-AND-Treasure fodder. Copied across the board each one is +N power AND a Treasure per creature — the 1/1s become threats and pay for the next spell.

staged.why: Medallion reduces GENERIC cost and a {R} cantrip has none — it is dead in a deck of one-mana fodder. Ancestral Anger is fodder that draws.
A 4-mana tutor that must survive and tap. Fodder that draws costs one.
Narrow artifact removal on a 4-drop body. Fodder that draws.
Five mana. Rile is the line you spotted: 1 damage to each of your own creatures, copied, and Pashalik Mons turns every Goblin death into damage at any target.
Random exile-and-play, not fodder, three mana. Accelerate is fodder that draws.
Spree modes the model cannot price and not fodder. Stun is fodder that draws.
A quest that needs four creatures before it does anything. Ground Rift is fodder AND has storm — copied twice over.
Five-mana body. The Helm gives Zada hexproof — which stops OPPONENTS targeting her and leaves your own cantrips legal. Shroud would switch her off.
Five-mana draw engine in a deck that wants to spend turn five killing. Mithril Coat has FLASH and auto-attaches to a legend: protection you hold up.
Lackey must connect before it does anything. Seething Anger is {R} fodder: +3/+0 copied across the whole board, with buyback {3} to do it again.
Snoop is card selection the deck no longer needs at 10 cantrips. The Archer turns every noncreature spell into 1 damage to EACH opponent — the conversion the branch measured as missing.
A 3-mana tutor for a Goblin in a deck that now wants to cast spells. Second per-cast damage body.
Grenzo needs combat damage first. Guttersnipe is 2 damage to each opponent per instant or sorcery — the biggest per-cast number in mono-red.
Cycling removal for one Goblin. The Boots are {1}, equip {1}, and give WARD {1} — strictly better than hexproof for Zada, because your own cantrips still target her freely and opponents have to pay.
Narrow artifact removal. The storm target assembles in 17.8% of games and the RITUAL leg is what is missing — Pyretic Ritual is {1}{R} for {R}{R}{R}, a net +1 and a storm count.
Impulse draw on a body, redundant now the deck draws 8 extra cards by T10. Desperate Ritual is the same net +1 ritual and splices onto Arcane.
A draw engine that needs tokens, in a deck that no longer needs help drawing. Rite of Flame is {R} for {R}{R} — the cheapest ritual in mono-red and it grows with each copy in any graveyard.
Ground Rift is fodder that neither draws nor pumps — 'can't block' is the weakest slot in the branch. Brute Force is {R} for +3/+3, and copied across seven bodies that is +21 power.
Buyback {3} almost never gets paid in a deck spending its mana on cantrips. Titan's Strength is the same {R} for +3/+1 AND scries.
A ritual for a pump, chosen over cutting a creature because Zada's copy count IS the body count. Monstrous Rage pumps +2/+0 AND leaves a permanent Monster Role (+1/+1 and trample) on the body.

Accelerate was HELD AND NEVER CAST in 60 Forge games — the AI drew it and passed. Reckless Ransacking is the same {1}{R} and does two jobs: +3/+2 across the board AND a Treasure per copy, which is the mana for the follow-up.
'Can't block' is the weakest rider in the branch. Sudden Breakthrough is +2/+0, first strike, and a Treasure per copy at the same {1}{R}.
